playstyle.label: tactical
playstyle.explanation: you trade or take pieces on 94% of your moves and your games run about 35 plies long - that is the biggest driver of your style.

strengths.headline: Your accuracy is trending up.
strengths.detail: Your average centipawn loss improved across the second half of your 13 games.

issues.headline: Blunders are your rating cap.
issues.diagnosis: You averaged 12.2 meaningful blunders per game across 13 games — at rating 920, that's the difference-maker in a 13-game sample; 25.2% came after move 25.
issues.prescription: Do 40 Lichess puzzles a day for 30 days, and before every move ask one question: what did their last move threaten?
issues.success_metric: Get your meaningful blunder rate from 12.2 to under 11.2 per game over your next 20 games.

issues.headline: Free pieces are walking away.
issues.diagnosis: 85.5% of your blunders left a piece where it could simply be taken — 136 hung-piece blunders in this batch.
issues.prescription: Board-vision drill: before moving, scan every undefended piece of yours; train the Lichess 'hanging pieces' theme for 15 minutes a day.
issues.success_metric: Cut hung-piece blunders from 85.5% to under 42.8% over your next 20 games.
issues.counter_evidence: This counts only positions where the opponent's best reply actually wins material.

issues.headline: You don't have a chess problem — you have a blitz problem.
issues.diagnosis: You don't have a chess problem — you have a blitz problem: 18.0 blunders per game in blitz vs 3.0 in rapid.
issues.prescription: Shift the ratio toward rapid for 30 days: play 3 rapid games for every 1 blitz game; blitz is testing, rapid is training.
issues.success_metric: Get your blitz blunder rate within 0.5 of your rapid rate over your next 20 games.
issues.counter_evidence: This only matters if you care about your rapid rating; in pure bullet practice the gap is expected.
